title.zh: 卷七十一 志第二十二: 禮樂五
title.raw: 卷七十一 志第二十二: 禮樂五 Volume 71 Treatises 24: Rites and Music 5

sentences.zh: 禮樂五 ○樂服樂正副四人，舒腳襆頭，紫羅公服，烏角帶，木笏，皂靴。

translations.literal: Rites and Music, Part Five ○ Ceremonial dress: four deputy music supervisors, spread-corner futou, purple gauze official robes, black horn belt, wooden tablets, and black boots.
translations.idiomatic: Rites and Music, Part Five ○ Ceremonial dress: the four deputy music supervisors wear spread-corner futou, purple gauze official robes, black horn belts, wooden tablets, and black boots.

sentences.zh: 照燭二人，服同前，無笏。

translations.literal: Two torchbearers: dress as above, but without tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Two torchbearers wear the same dress as above but carry no tablets.

sentences.zh: 樂師二人，服緋，冠、笏同前。

translations.literal: Two music masters: scarlet dress; caps and tablets as above.
translations.idiomatic: Two music masters wear scarlet robes, with caps and tablets like those above.

sentences.zh: 運譜二人，服綠，冠、笏同前。

translations.literal: Two score keepers: green dress; caps and tablets as above.
translations.idiomatic: Two score keepers wear green robes, with caps and tablets like those above.

sentences.zh: 舞師二人，舒腳襆頭，黃羅繡抹額，紫服，金銅荔枝帶，皂靴，各執仗。

translations.literal: Two dance masters: spread-corner futou, yellow gauze embroidered forehead bands, purple robes, gold-and-copper lychee belts, black boots; each holds a staff.
translations.idiomatic: Two dance masters wear spread-corner futou, yellow gauze embroidered forehead bands, purple robes, gold-and-copper lychee belts, and black boots, each bearing a staff.

sentences.zh: （仗，牙仗也。）〉

translations.literal: (The staffs are yak-tail staffs.)
translations.idiomatic: (The staffs are yak-tail ceremonial staffs.)

sentences.zh: 執旌二人，平冕，前後各九旒五就，青生色鸞袍，黃綾帶，黃絹袴，白絹襪，赤革履。

translations.literal: Two banner bearers: even coronets, nine tassels with five clusters before and behind; green unpatterned luan robes, yellow gauze belts, yellow silk trousers, white silk socks, and red leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Two banner bearers wear even coronets with nine tassels of five clusters fore and aft, green unpatterned luan robes, yellow gauze belts, yellow silk trousers, white silk socks, and red leather shoes.

sentences.zh: （平冕鸞袍，皆仿金制，惟冕之旒數不同，詳見後至元二年博士議。）〉

translations.literal: (The even coronet and luan robe both follow Jin practice, save that the number of tassels on the coronet differs; see the doctors' deliberation of the second year of the Later Zhiyuan era for details.)
translations.idiomatic: (The even coronet and luan robe follow Jin models, except that the coronet's tassels differ in number; see the doctors' deliberation of the second year of the Later Zhiyuan era for particulars.)

sentences.zh: 執纛二人，青羅巾，余同執旌。

translations.literal: Two standard bearers: blue gauze caps; the rest as for banner bearers.
translations.idiomatic: Two standard bearers wear blue gauze caps; their other dress matches the banner bearers.

sentences.zh: 樂工，介幘冠，緋羅生色鸞袍，黃綾帶，皂靴。

translations.literal: Musicians: jieze caps, scarlet gauze unpatterned luan robes, yellow gauze belts, and black boots.
translations.idiomatic: Musicians wear jieze caps, scarlet gauze unpatterned luan robes, yellow gauze belts, and black boots.

sentences.zh: （冠以皮為之，黑油如熊耳，亦金制也。）〉

translations.literal: (The cap is made of leather, black-lacquered like bear ears; this too is Jin practice.)
translations.idiomatic: (The cap is of leather, lacquered black like bear ears—also a Jin model.)

sentences.zh: 歌工，服同樂工。

translations.literal: Singers: dress as musicians.
translations.idiomatic: Singers wear the same dress as the musicians.

sentences.zh: 執麾，服同上，惟加平巾幘。

translations.literal: Banner-pole bearers: dress as above, but with the addition of plain-cloth jieze.
translations.idiomatic: Banner-pole bearers dress as above but also wear plain-cloth jieze.

sentences.zh: （狀若籠金幘，以革為之。）〉

translations.literal: (In shape like a gilded cage-cap; made of leather.)
translations.idiomatic: (Shaped like a gilded cage-cap and made of leather.)

sentences.zh: 舞人，青羅生色義花鸞袍，緣以皂綾，平冕冠。

translations.literal: Dancers: green gauze unpatterned righteousness-flower luan robes, bordered with black gauze, and even coronets.
translations.idiomatic: Dancers wear green gauze unpatterned righteousness-flower luan robes trimmed with black gauze and even coronets.

sentences.zh: （冠前後有旒，青白硝石珠相間。）〉

translations.literal: (The coronet has tassels before and behind, with blue and white crystal beads alternating.)
translations.idiomatic: (The coronet bears tassels fore and aft, strung with alternating blue and white crystal beads.)

sentences.zh: 執器二十人，服同樂工，綠油母追冠，

translations.literal: Twenty instrument bearers: dress as musicians, green-lacquered leather muzhui caps,
translations.idiomatic: Twenty instrument bearers dress as musicians and wear green-lacquered leather muzhui caps,

sentences.zh: （革為之，一名武弁。）〉

translations.literal: (Made of leather; also called the martial cap.)
translations.idiomatic: (Made of leather and also known as the martial cap.)

sentences.zh: 加紅抹額。

translations.literal: with red forehead bands added.
translations.idiomatic: with red forehead bands added.

sentences.zh: 至元二年閏五月，大樂署言，堂上下樂舞官員及樂工，合用衣服冠冕靴履等物，乞行制造。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fifth month of the second year of Zhiyuan, the Office of Great Music reported that the music and dance officers above and below the hall, together with the musicians, required robes, caps, crowns, boots, and shoes, and requested that these be manufactured.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month of the second year of Zhiyuan, the Office of Great Music reported that the music and dance officers above and below the hall, together with the musicians, needed robes, caps, crowns, boots, and shoes, and asked that they be made.

sentences.zh: 太常寺下博士議定：樂正副四人、樂師二人、照燭二人、運譜二人，皆服紫羅公服，皂紗襆頭舒腳，紅鞓角帶，木笏，皂靴。

translations.literal: The doctors under the Grand Secretariat of Rites deliberated and fixed: four deputy music supervisors, two music masters, two torchbearers, and two score keepers—all wear purple gauze official robes, black gauze futou with spread corners, red leather horn belts, wooden tablets, and black boots.
translations.idiomatic: The doctors under the Grand Secretariat of Rites determined that the four deputy music supervisors, two music masters, two torchbearers, and two score keepers should all wear purple gauze official robes, black gauze futou with spread corners, red leather horn belts, wooden tablets, and black boots.

sentences.zh: 引舞色長四人，紫羅公服，皂紗襆頭展腳，黃羅繡南花抹額，金銅帶，皂靴。

translations.literal: Four lead-dance section chiefs: purple gauze official robes, black gauze futou with extended corners, yellow gauze embroidered southern-flower forehead bands, gold-and-copper belts, and black boots.
translations.idiomatic: Four lead-dance section chiefs wear purple gauze official robes, black gauze futou with extended corners, yellow gauze embroidered southern-flower forehead bands, gold-and-copper belts, and black boots.

sentences.zh: 樂工二百四十有六人，緋繡義花鸞袍，縣黃插口，介幘冠，紫羅帶，全黃羅抹帶，黃絹夾褲，白綾襪，朱履。

translations.literal: Two hundred forty-six musicians: scarlet embroidered righteousness-flower luan robes, with yellow hanging mouth-pieces, jieze caps, purple gauze belts, full yellow gauze forehead bands, yellow silk lined trousers, white gauze socks, and red shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred forty-six musicians wear scarlet embroidered righteousness-flower luan robes with yellow hanging mouth-pieces, jieze caps, purple gauze belts, full yellow gauze forehead bands, yellow silk lined trousers, white gauze socks, and red shoes.

sentences.zh: （金太常寺掌故張珍所著《疊代世範》載金制：舞人服黑衫，皆四襖，有黃插口，左右垂之，黃綾抹帶，其衫以綢為之，胸背二答、兩肩二答，前後和一答，皆彩色，繡二鸞盤飛之狀，綴之於衫。

translations.literal: (Zhang Zhen, archivist of the Jin Grand Secretariat of Rites, records Jin practice in his 《Successive Ages as Models》: dancers wore black jackets, all four-layered, with yellow mouth-pieces hanging to left and right, and yellow gauze forehead bands; the jackets were of silk, with two plaques on chest and back, two on each shoulder, and one joining front and back—all in colors, embroidered with paired luan in coiling flight, sewn onto the jacket.
translations.idiomatic: (In Zhang Zhen's 《Successive Ages as Models》, archivist of the Jin Grand Secretariat of Rites, Jin dancers wore black four-layered jackets with yellow mouth-pieces hanging at the sides and yellow gauze forehead bands. The jackets were silk, bearing colored plaques on chest and back, on each shoulder, and joining front and back, all embroidered with paired luan in coiling flight and sewn to the garment.

sentences.zh: 冠以平冕，亦有天板、口圈，天門納言以紫絹標背，銅裹邊圈，前後各五旒，以青白硝石珠相間。

translations.literal: The cap was an even coronet, also with a heaven-board and mouth-ring; the heaven-gate and speech-ribbon were marked on purple silk backing, with a copper-clad rim; five tassels before and behind, with blue and white crystal beads alternating.
translations.idiomatic: They wore even coronets with heaven-board and mouth-ring; the heaven-gate and speech-ribbon were backed in purple silk with a copper-clad rim, and five tassels fore and aft strung with alternating blue and white crystal beads.

sentences.zh: 《大備集》所載，二舞人皂繡義花鸞衫，縣紫插口，黃綾抹帶，朱履，平冕。

translations.literal: The 《Great Completeness Collection》 records two dancers in black embroidered righteousness-flower luan jackets, with purple hanging mouth-pieces, yellow gauze forehead bands, red shoes, and even coronets.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Great Completeness Collection》 describes two dancers in black embroidered righteousness-flower luan jackets with purple hanging mouth-pieces, yellow gauze forehead bands, red shoes, and even coronets.

sentences.zh: 其冠有口圈，亦有天門納言系帶，口圈高一尺許，天板長二尺，闊一尺，前微高後低，裏外紫絹糊，銅楞道妝釘，無旒。）〉

translations.literal: (Their coronets had mouth-rings and heaven-gate speech-ribbons with ties; the mouth-ring was about a foot high; the heaven-board two feet long and one foot wide, slightly higher in front and lower behind, lined inside and out with purple silk, with copper ribbing and ornamental nails, and no tassels.)
translations.idiomatic: (Their coronets had mouth-rings and heaven-gate speech-ribbons with ties. The mouth-ring stood about a foot high; the heaven-board was two feet long and one foot wide, slightly higher in front than behind, lined inside and out with purple silk and studded with copper ribbing, and bore no tassels.)

sentences.zh: 執器二十人，緋繡義花鸞袍，縣黃插口，綠油革冠，黃羅抹帶，黃絹夾褲，白綾襪，朱履。

translations.literal: Twenty instrument bearers: scarlet embroidered righteousness-flower luan robes, with yellow hanging mouth-pieces, green-lacquered leather caps, yellow gauze forehead bands, yellow silk lined trousers, white gauze socks, and red shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty instrument bearers wear scarlet embroidered righteousness-flower luan robes with yellow hanging mouth-pieces, green-lacquered leather caps, yellow gauze forehead bands, yellow silk lined trousers, white gauze socks, and red shoes.

sentences.zh: 旌纛四人，青繡義花鸞袍，縣紫插口，平冕冠二，青包巾二，黃羅抹帶，黃絹夾褲，白綾襪，朱履。

translations.literal: Four banner-and-standard bearers: green embroidered righteousness-flower luan robes, with purple hanging mouth-pieces; two even coronets, two blue wrapped caps; yellow gauze forehead bands, yellow silk lined trousers, white gauze socks, and red shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Four banner-and-standard bearers wear green embroidered righteousness-flower luan robes with purple hanging mouth-pieces; two wear even coronets and two blue wrapped caps, with yellow gauze forehead bands, yellow silk lined trousers, white gauze socks, and red shoes.

sentences.zh: 七月，中書吏部再準太常博士議定，行下所司制造。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, the Secretariat's Ministry of Personnel again approved the doctors' deliberation of the Grand Secretariat of Rites and ordered the responsible offices to manufacture them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Secretariat's Ministry of Personnel again ratified the Grand Secretariat doctors' decision and ordered the responsible offices to manufacture the garments.

sentences.zh: 三年九月服成，緋鸞袍二百六十有七，青鸞袍一百三十二，黃絹褲一百五十二，紫羅公服一十四，黃綾帶三百九十七，介幘冠二百四十有四，平冕冠百三十，簪全，木笏十有六，襆頭十有四，平巾幘二，綠油革冠二十，荔枝銅帶四，角帶十，皂靴二百六十對，朱履百五十對。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year the garments were complete: two hundred sixty-seven scarlet luan robes, one hundred thirty-two green luan robes, one hundred fifty-two pairs of yellow silk trousers, fourteen purple gauze official robes, three hundred ninety-seven yellow gauze belts, two hundred forty-four jieze caps, one hundred thirty even coronets with hairpins complete, sixteen wooden tablets, fourteen futou, two plain-cloth jieze, twenty green-lacquered leather caps, four lychee copper belts, ten horn belts, two hundred sixty pairs of black boots, and one hundred fifty pairs of red shoes.
translations.idiomatic: By the ninth month of the third year the garments were finished: 267 scarlet luan robes, 132 green luan robes, 152 pairs of yellow silk trousers, 14 purple gauze official robes, 397 yellow gauze belts, 244 jieze caps, 130 even coronets with hairpins, 16 wooden tablets, 14 futou, 2 plain-cloth jieze, 20 green-lacquered leather caps, 4 lychee copper belts, 10 horn belts, 260 pairs of black boots, and 150 pairs of red shoes.

sentences.zh: 宣聖廟樂工，黑漆冠三十五，綠羅生色胸背花袍三十五，皂靴三十五對，黃絹囊三十五，黃絹夾袱三十五。

translations.literal: Musicians at the Temple of the Sagely Exemplar: thirty-five black-lacquered caps, thirty-five green gauze unpatterned chest-and-back flower robes, thirty-five pairs of black boots, thirty-five yellow silk pouches, and thirty-five yellow silk lined wrappers.
translations.idiomatic: For musicians at the Temple of the Sagely Exemplar there were 35 black-lacquered caps, 35 green gauze unpatterned chest-and-back flower robes, 35 pairs of black boots, 35 yellow silk pouches, and 35 yellow silk lined wrappers.

sentences.zh: 大樂職掌

translations.literal: Duties of the Office of Great Music
translations.idiomatic: Duties of the Office of Great Music

sentences.zh: 大樂署，令一人，丞一人，掌郊社、宗廟之樂。

translations.literal: The Office of Great Music had one director and one assistant director, charged with music for suburban altars and the imperial ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: The Office of Great Music had one director and one assistant director, responsible for music at suburban altars and the imperial ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 凡樂，郊社、宗廟則用宮縣，工四百六十有一人；

translations.literal: In general for music: suburban altars and the ancestral temple used the court ensemble, with four hundred sixty-one workers;
translations.idiomatic: For music generally, suburban altars and the ancestral temple employed the full court ensemble with 461 performers;

sentences.zh: 社稷，則用登歌，工五十有一人；

translations.literal: for the altars of soil and grain, ascending-hall music was used, with fifty-one workers;
translations.idiomatic: the altars of soil and grain used ascending-hall music with 51 performers;

sentences.zh: 二樂用工三百一十有二人，代事故者五十人。

translations.literal: the two kinds of music together required three hundred twelve workers, with fifty substitutes for those who fell ill or died.
translations.idiomatic: both forms together required 312 workers, with 50 substitutes for illness or death.

sentences.zh: 前祭之月，召工習樂及舞。

translations.literal: In the month before a sacrifice, the workers were summoned to rehearse music and dance.
translations.idiomatic: In the month before a sacrifice, performers were summoned to rehearse music and dance.

sentences.zh: 祀前一日，宿縣於庭中。

translations.literal: On the day before the rite, the suspended ensemble was lodged overnight in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the rite, the suspended ensemble was set up overnight in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 東方西方設十二镈鐘，各依辰位。

translations.literal: East and west, twelve bo bells were set out, each according to its earthly-branch position.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve bo bells were placed east and west, each aligned with its earthly-branch station.

sentences.zh: 編鐘處其左，編磬處其右。

translations.literal: Chime-bells were placed to their left, chime-stones to their right.
translations.idiomatic: Chime-bells stood to their left and chime-stones to their right.

sentences.zh: 黃鐘之鐘起子位，在通街之西。

translations.literal: The bell of the Yellow Bell pitch began at the zi position, west of the central street.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Bell bell began at the zi station, west of the central street.

sentences.zh: 蕤賓之鐘居午位，在通街之東。

translations.literal: The bell of the Luxuriant Guest pitch occupied the wu position, east of the central street.
translations.idiomatic: The Luxuriant Guest bell occupied the wu station, east of the central street.

sentences.zh: 每辰三虡，謂之一肆，十有二辰，凡三十六虡。

translations.literal: For each earthly branch there were three frames, called one spread; twelve branches in all made thirty-six frames.
translations.idiomatic: Each earthly branch had three frames, called one spread; twelve branches yielded thirty-six frames in all.

sentences.zh: 樹建鞞應於四隅，左右，設縣中之北。

translations.literal: Bian and ying drums were erected at the four corners; left and right, they were set north of the center of the suspended ensemble.
translations.idiomatic: Bian and ying drums were set at the four corners; to left and right they stood north of the ensemble's center.

sentences.zh: 歌工次之，

translations.literal: Singers came next,
translations.idiomatic: Next came the singers,

sentences.zh: （三十二人，重行相向而坐。）〉

translations.literal: (thirty-two persons, seated in double ranks facing one another.)
translations.idiomatic: (thirty-two in all, seated in double ranks facing one another.)

sentences.zh: 巢笙次之，簫次之，竽次之，籥次之，篪次之，塤次之，長笛又次之。

translations.literal: then nest-sheng, then xiao, then yu, then yue, then chi, then xun, and long flutes again after that.
translations.idiomatic: then nest-sheng, xiao, yu, yue, chi, xun, and long flutes in that order.

sentences.zh: 夾街之左右，瑟翼敔之東西，在前行。

translations.literal: To left and right along the flanking streets, se flanked the yi east and west, in the front rank.
translations.idiomatic: Along the flanking streets to left and right, se flanked the yi east and west in the front rank.

sentences.zh: 路鼓、路鼗次之。

translations.literal: Road drums and road tambourines came next.
translations.idiomatic: Road drums and road tambourines came next.

sentences.zh: （郊祀則雷鼓、雷鼗。）〉

translations.literal: (For suburban sacrifice, thunder drums and thunder tambourines were used.)
translations.idiomatic: (At suburban sacrifice, thunder drums and thunder tambourines were used instead.)

sentences.zh: 閏余匏在簫之東，七星匏在西，九曜匏次之。

translations.literal: The intercalary-surplus gourd-pipe was east of the xiao; the Seven Stars gourd-pipe was west; the Nine Luminaries gourd-pipe came after it.
translations.idiomatic: The intercalary-surplus gourd-pipe stood east of the xiao; the Seven Stars gourd-pipe to the west; the Nine Luminaries gourd-pipe followed.

sentences.zh: 一弦琴列路鼓之東西，

translations.literal: One-string zithers were arrayed east and west of the road drums,
translations.idiomatic: One-string zithers were placed east and west of the road drums,

sentences.zh: （東一，西二。）〉

translations.literal: (one in the east, two in the west.)
translations.idiomatic: (one in the east, two in the west.)

sentences.zh: 三弦、五弦、七弦、九弦次之。

translations.literal: three-string, five-string, seven-string, and nine-string zithers came after.
translations.idiomatic: followed by three-, five-, seven-, and nine-string zithers.

sentences.zh: 晉鼓一，處縣中之東南，以節樂。

translations.literal: One Jin drum stood southeast of the center of the suspended ensemble to mark the beat.
translations.idiomatic: A single Jin drum stood southeast of the ensemble's center to mark the beat.

sentences.zh: （一弦琴三，五弦以下皆六。

translations.literal: (Three one-string zithers; six each of five-string and below.
translations.idiomatic: (Three one-string zithers; six each of five-string and below.

sentences.zh: 凡坐者，高以杌，地以氈。）〉

translations.literal: (All who sat were raised on stools and the ground was covered with felt.)
translations.idiomatic: (All seated players used stools, with felt spread on the ground.)

sentences.zh: 立四表於橫街之南，少東。

translations.literal: Four marker poles were erected south of the cross street, slightly east.
translations.idiomatic: Four marker poles were set up south of the cross street, slightly to the east.

sentences.zh: 設舞位於縣北。

translations.literal: Dance positions were set north of the suspended ensemble.
translations.idiomatic: Dance positions were laid out north of the suspended ensemble.

sentences.zh: 文郎左執籥，右秉翟；

translations.literal: Civil dancers held yue in the left hand and feathers in the right;
translations.idiomatic: Civil dancers held yue in the left hand and feathers in the right;

sentences.zh: 武郎左執幹，右執戚；

translations.literal: martial dancers held shields in the left hand and axes in the right;
translations.idiomatic: martial dancers held shields in the left and axes in the right;

sentences.zh: 皆六十有四人。

translations.literal: sixty-four in all.
translations.idiomatic: sixty-four in all.

sentences.zh: 享日，與工人先入就位。

translations.literal: On the day of the offering, they entered with the workers beforehand and took their places.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the offering, they entered ahead of the other performers and took their stations.

sentences.zh: 舞師二人，執纛二人，引文舞分立於表南。

translations.literal: Two dance masters and two standard bearers led the civil dance, which stood in separate ranks south of the markers.
translations.idiomatic: Two dance masters and two standard bearers led the civil dancers, who stood in separate ranks south of the markers.

sentences.zh: 武舞及執器者，俟立於宮縣之左右。

translations.literal: The martial dance and instrument bearers waited, standing to left and right of the court ensemble.
translations.idiomatic: The martial dancers and instrument bearers waited on either side of the court ensemble.

sentences.zh: 器鼗二，雙鐸二，單鐸二，鐃二，錞二，

translations.literal: two instrument tambourines, two paired bells, two single bells, two nao, two zheng,
translations.idiomatic: two instrument tambourines, two paired bells, two single bells, two nao, two zheng,

sentences.zh: （二錞用六人。）〉

translations.literal: (The two zheng required six persons.)
translations.idiomatic: (The two zheng required six players.)

sentences.zh: 鉦二，相鼓二，雅鼓二，凡二十人。

translations.literal: two gongs, two xiang drums, two ya drums—twenty persons in all.
translations.idiomatic: two gongs, two xiang drums, and two ya drums—twenty players in all.

sentences.zh: 文舞退，舞師二人、執旌二人，引武舞進，立其處，文舞還立於縣側。

translations.literal: When the civil dance withdrew, two dance masters and two banner bearers led the martial dance forward to stand in their place, and the civil dance returned to stand beside the suspended ensemble.
translations.idiomatic: When the civil dance withdrew, two dance masters and two banner bearers led the martial dance forward to take their place, while the civil dancers returned to stand beside the suspended ensemble.

sentences.zh: 又設登歌樂於殿之前楹，

translations.literal: Ascending-hall music was also set at the front eaves of the hall,
translations.idiomatic: Ascending-hall music was also arranged at the front eaves of the hall,

sentences.zh: （殿陛之旁，設樂床二，樂工列於上。）〉

translations.literal: (beside the hall steps, two music platforms were set up, with musicians arrayed upon them.)
translations.idiomatic: (beside the hall steps stood two music platforms, with musicians arrayed on them.)

sentences.zh: 搏拊二，歌工六，一，一，在門內，相向而坐。

translations.literal: two bofu, six singers—one here, one there—inside the gate, seated facing one another.
translations.idiomatic: two bofu and six singers—three to a side—seated inside the gate facing one another.

sentences.zh: 鐘一虡，在前楹之東。

translations.literal: One frame of bells stood east of the front eaves.
translations.idiomatic: One frame of bells stood east of the front eaves.

sentences.zh: 一弦、三弦、五弦、七弦、九弦琴五，次之。

translations.literal: Five zithers—one-string, three-string, five-string, seven-string, and nine-string—came after.
translations.idiomatic: Five zithers—one-, three-, five-, seven-, and nine-string—followed.

sentences.zh: 瑟二，在其東，笛一、籥一、篪一在琴之南，巢笙、和笙各二次之。

translations.literal: Two se to their east; one flute, one yue, and one chi south of the zithers; nest-sheng and he-sheng, two each, came after.
translations.idiomatic: Two se stood east of them; one flute, one yue, and one chi south of the zithers; nest-sheng and he-sheng, two each, followed.

sentences.zh: 塤一，在笛之南。

translations.literal: One xun south of the flute.
translations.idiomatic: One xun stood south of the flute.

sentences.zh: 閏余匏、排簫各一，次之，皆西上。

translations.literal: One intercalary-surplus gourd-pipe and one panpipe came after, all ascending to the west.
translations.idiomatic: One intercalary-surplus gourd-pipe and one panpipe followed, all ranked ascending to the west.

sentences.zh: 磬一虡，在前楹之西。

translations.literal: One frame of chime-stones stood west of the front eaves.
translations.idiomatic: One frame of chime-stones stood west of the front eaves.

sentences.zh: 一弦、三弦、五弦、七弦、九弦琴五，次之。

translations.literal: Five zithers—one-string, three-string, five-string, seven-string, and nine-string—came after.
translations.idiomatic: Five zithers—one-, three-, five-, seven-, and nine-string—followed.

sentences.zh: 塤一，在笛之南。

translations.literal: One xun south of the flute.
translations.idiomatic: One xun stood south of the flute.

sentences.zh: 七星匏、九曜匏、排簫各一，次之，皆東上。

translations.literal: One Seven Stars gourd-pipe, one Nine Luminaries gourd-pipe, and one panpipe came after, all ascending to the east.
translations.idiomatic: One Seven Stars gourd-pipe, one Nine Luminaries gourd-pipe, and one panpipe followed, all ranked ascending to the east.

sentences.zh: 凡宗廟之樂九成，舞九變。

translations.literal: In general, music for the ancestral temple had nine movements, and the dance had nine changes.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestral temple music comprised nine movements, with nine dance changes.

sentences.zh: 黃鐘之宮，三成，三變。

translations.literal: The Yellow Bell mode: three movements, three changes.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Bell mode: three movements and three dance changes.

sentences.zh: 大呂之角，二成，二變。

translations.literal: The Great Clarity second mode: two movements, two changes.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Clarity second mode: two movements and two changes.

sentences.zh: 太簇之徵，二成，二變。

translations.literal: The Great Cluster third mode: two movements, two changes.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Cluster third mode: two movements and two changes.

sentences.zh: 應鐘之羽，二成，二變。

translations.literal: The Responding Bell fifth mode: two movements, two changes.
translations.idiomatic: The Responding Bell fifth mode: two movements and two changes.

sentences.zh: 圜丘之樂六成，舞六變。

translations.literal: Music for the Circular Mound had six movements, and the dance had six changes.
translations.idiomatic: Music at the Circular Mound comprised six movements, with six dance changes.

sentences.zh: 夾鐘之宮，三成，三變。

translations.literal: The Pinched Bell mode: three movements, three changes.
translations.idiomatic: The Pinched Bell mode: three movements and three dance changes.

sentences.zh: 黃鐘之角，一成，一變。

translations.literal: The Yellow Bell second mode: one movement, one change.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Bell second mode: one movement and one change.

sentences.zh: 太簇之徵，一成，一變。

translations.literal: The Great Cluster third mode: one movement, one change.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Cluster third mode: one movement and one change.

sentences.zh: 姑洗之羽，一成，一變。

translations.literal: The Maiden Wash fifth mode: one movement, one change.
translations.idiomatic: The Maiden Wash fifth mode: one movement and one change.

sentences.zh: 社稷之樂八成：林鐘之宮二成，太簇之角二成，姑洗之征二成，南呂之羽二成。

translations.literal: Music for the altars of soil and grain had eight movements: two in the Forest Bell mode, two in the Great Cluster second mode, two in the Maiden Wash third mode, and two in the Southern Pitch fifth mode.
translations.idiomatic: Music at the altars of soil and grain had eight movements: two in the Forest Bell mode, two in the Great Cluster second mode, two in the Maiden Wash third mode, and two in the Southern Pitch fifth mode.

sentences.zh: 凡有事於宗廟，大樂令位於殿楹之東，西向；

translations.literal: Whenever there was business at the ancestral temple, the Director of Great Music took his post east of the hall eaves, facing west;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever rites were held at the ancestral temple, the Director of Great Music stood east of the hall eaves, facing west;

sentences.zh: 丞位於縣北，通街之東，西向；

translations.literal: the assistant director stood north of the suspended ensemble, east of the central street, facing west;
translations.idiomatic: the assistant director stood north of the suspended ensemble, east of the central street, facing west;

sentences.zh: 以肅樂舞。

translations.literal: to keep music and dance in order.
translations.idiomatic: to keep the music and dance in proper order.

sentences.zh: 協律郎二人，掌和律呂，以合陰陽之聲。

translations.literal: Two Pitch-Pipe Masters were charged with harmonizing the pitch-pipes and tubes to unite the sounds of yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: Two Pitch-Pipe Masters harmonized the pitch-pipes and tubes so that the sounds of yin and yang would accord.

sentences.zh: 陽律六：黃鐘子，太簇寅，姑洗辰，蕤賓午，夷則申，無射戌。

translations.literal: The six yang pitch-pipes: Yellow Bell at zi, Great Cluster at yin, Maiden Wash at chen, Luxuriant Guest at wu, Levelled Rule at shen, and Unshot at xu.
translations.idiomatic: The six yang pitch-pipes were Yellow Bell at zi, Great Cluster at yin, Maiden Wash at chen, Luxuriant Guest at wu, Levelled Rule at shen, and Unshot at xu.

sentences.zh: 陰呂六：大呂醜，夾鐘卯，仲呂巳，林鐘未，南呂酉，應鐘亥。

translations.literal: The six yin tubes: Great Clarity at chou, Pinched Bell at mao, Second Pitch at si, Forest Bell at wei, Southern Pitch at you, and Responding Bell at hai.
translations.idiomatic: The six yin tubes were Great Clarity at chou, Pinched Bell at mao, Second Pitch at si, Forest Bell at wei, Southern Pitch at you, and Responding Bell at hai.

sentences.zh: 文之以宮、商、角、徵、羽、變宮、變徵，播之以金、石、絲、竹、匏、土、革、木。

translations.literal: They were patterned with gong, shang, jue, zhi, yu, altered gong, and altered zhi, and disseminated through metal, stone, silk, bamboo, gourd, earth, leather, and wood.
translations.idiomatic: They were patterned with the seven modes—gong, shang, jue, zhi, yu, altered gong, and altered zhi—and disseminated through the eight materials: metal, stone, silk, bamboo, gourd, earth, leather, and wood.

sentences.zh: 凡律管之數九，九九相乘，八十一以為宮；

translations.literal: The number for pitch-pipes was nine; nine times nine made eighty-one for gong;
translations.idiomatic: Pitch-pipes were reckoned by nines; nine times nine yielded eighty-one for the gong tone;

sentences.zh: 三分去一，五十四以為徵；

translations.literal: one-third removed left fifty-four for zhi;
translations.idiomatic: removing one-third left fifty-four for zhi;

sentences.zh: 三分益一，七十二以為商；

translations.literal: one-third added made seventy-two for shang;
translations.idiomatic: adding one-third made seventy-two for shang;

sentences.zh: 三分去一，四十八以為羽；

translations.literal: one-third removed left forty-eight for yu;
translations.idiomatic: removing one-third left forty-eight for yu;

sentences.zh: 三分益一，六十四以為角。

translations.literal: one-third added made sixty-four for jue.
translations.idiomatic: adding one-third made sixty-four for jue.

sentences.zh: 如黃鐘為宮，則林鐘為徵，太簇為商，南呂為羽，姑洗為角，應鐘為變宮，蕤賓為變征，是為七聲十二律，還相為宮，為八十四調。

translations.literal: If Yellow Bell served as gong, then Forest Bell was zhi, Great Cluster was shang, Southern Pitch was yu, Maiden Wash was jue, Responding Bell was altered gong, and Luxuriant Guest was altered zhi—thus the seven tones and twelve pitch-standards, each in turn serving as gong, made eighty-four modes.
translations.idiomatic: When Yellow Bell served as gong, Forest Bell was zhi, Great Cluster shang, Southern Pitch yu, Maiden Wash jue, Responding Bell altered gong, and Luxuriant Guest altered zhi—yielding the seven tones and twelve pitch-standards, each in turn serving as gong, for eighty-four modes in all.

sentences.zh: 凡大祭祀皆法服，一人立於殿楹之西，東向；

translations.literal: At every great sacrifice all wore ritual dress; one person stood west of the hall eaves, facing east;
translations.idiomatic: At every great sacrifice all wore ritual dress; one person stood west of the hall eaves, facing east;

sentences.zh: 一人立於縣北通街之西，東向；

translations.literal: one stood west of the central street north of the suspended ensemble, facing east;
translations.idiomatic: another stood west of the central street north of the suspended ensemble, facing east;

sentences.zh: 以節樂。

translations.literal: to mark the music.
translations.idiomatic: to mark the music.

sentences.zh: （堂上者主登歌，堂下者主宮縣。）〉

translations.literal: (The one above the hall directed ascending-hall music; the one below directed the court ensemble.)
translations.idiomatic: (The one above the hall directed ascending-hall music; the one below directed the court ensemble.)

sentences.zh: 凡樂作，則跪，俯伏，舉麾以興，工鼓以奏；

translations.literal: Whenever music began, they knelt and prostrated themselves, raised the banner to start it, and the workers drummed to play;
translations.idiomatic: When music began, they knelt and prostrated themselves, raised the banner to start it, and the musicians drummed to play;

sentences.zh: 樂止則偃麾，工戛而樂止。

translations.literal: when it stopped they lowered the banner, and the workers struck the yi and the music ceased.
translations.idiomatic: when it stopped they lowered the banner, and the musicians struck the yi to end the music.

sentences.zh: （今執麾者代執之，協律郎特拜而已。）〉

translations.literal: (Now the banner-pole bearer performs this in their stead; the Pitch-Pipe Master only performs the special bow.)
translations.idiomatic: (Nowadays the banner-pole bearer does this in their place; the Pitch-Pipe Master only performs the special bow.)

sentences.zh: 樂正二人，副二人，掌肄樂舞、展樂器、正樂位。

translations.literal: Two music supervisors and two assistants were charged with drilling music and dance, deploying instruments, and correcting musical positions.
translations.idiomatic: Two music supervisors and two assistants drilled music and dance, deployed instruments, and corrected the performers' stations.

sentences.zh: 凡祭，二人立於殿內，二人立於縣間，以節樂。

translations.literal: At every sacrifice, two stood inside the hall and two between the suspended ensembles, to mark the music.
translations.idiomatic: At every sacrifice, two stood inside the hall and two between the suspended ensembles to regulate the music.

sentences.zh: 殿內者視獻者奠獻用樂作止之節，以笏示照燭，照燭舉偃以示堂下。

translations.literal: Those inside the hall watched the offering-official's rhythm for starting and stopping music at presentation, signaled the torchbearers with their tablets, and the torchbearers raised or lowered them to show those below the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Those inside the hall watched the offering-official's cues for starting and stopping the music, signaled the torchbearers with their tablets, and the torchbearers raised or lowered their lights to signal those below.

sentences.zh: 若作登歌，則以笏示敔而已。

translations.literal: If ascending-hall music was performed, they signaled only the yi with their tablets.
translations.idiomatic: When ascending-hall music was played, they signaled only the yi with their tablets.

sentences.zh: 縣間者視堂上照燭。

translations.literal: Those between the ensembles watched the torchbearers above the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Those between the ensembles watched the torchbearers in the hall above.

sentences.zh: 及引初獻，照燭動，亦以笏示敔。

translations.literal: When leading the first offering-official, as the torchbearers moved, they likewise signaled the yi with their tablets.
translations.idiomatic: When leading the first offering-official, as the torchbearers moved, they likewise signaled the yi with their tablets.

sentences.zh: 樂師一人，運譜一人，掌以樂教工人。

translations.literal: One music master and one score keeper were charged with teaching the workers through music.
translations.idiomatic: One music master and one score keeper taught the musicians their parts.

sentences.zh: 凡祭，立於縣間，皆北上，相向而立。

translations.literal: At every sacrifice they stood between the ensembles, all facing north, standing opposite one another.
translations.idiomatic: At every sacrifice they stood between the ensembles, all facing north and opposite one another.

sentences.zh: 舞師四人，皆執梃，

translations.literal: Four dance masters, all holding staffs,
translations.idiomatic: Four dance masters, each bearing a staff,

sentences.zh: （梃，牙仗也。）〉

translations.literal: (The staffs are yak-tail staffs.)
translations.idiomatic: (The staffs are yak-tail ceremonial staffs.)

sentences.zh: 執纛二人，執旌二人，祭則前舉以為舞容。

translations.literal: two standard bearers and two banner bearers; at the sacrifice they led the way, raising them to set the dance formation.
translations.idiomatic: two standard bearers and two banner bearers; at the sacrifice they led the way, raising them to shape the dance formation.

sentences.zh: 舞人從南表向第一表，為一成，則一變；

translations.literal: Dancers moved from the southern marker toward the first marker—one movement, one change;
translations.idiomatic: Dancers moved from the southern marker to the first marker—one movement, one change;

sentences.zh: 從第二至第三，為二成；

translations.literal: from the second to the third was two movements;
translations.idiomatic: from the second to the third was two movements;

sentences.zh: 從第三至北第四表，為三成；

translations.literal: from the third to the fourth northern marker was three movements;
translations.idiomatic: from the third to the fourth northern marker was three movements;

sentences.zh: 舞人各轉身南向於北表之北，還從第一至第二，為四成；

translations.literal: each dancer turned south at the north of the northern marker, then returned from the first to the second—four movements;
translations.idiomatic: each dancer turned south beyond the northern marker, then returned from the first to the second marker—four movements;

sentences.zh: 從第二至第三，為五成；

translations.literal: from the second to the third was five movements;
translations.idiomatic: from the second to the third was five movements;

sentences.zh: 從第三至南第一表，為六成；

translations.literal: from the third to the first southern marker was six movements;
translations.idiomatic: from the third to the first southern marker was six movements;

sentences.zh: 若八變者，更從南北向第二，為七成；

translations.literal: for eight changes, they again moved from south to north toward the second—seven movements;
translations.idiomatic: for eight changes, they again moved from south to north toward the second marker—seven movements;

sentences.zh: 又從第二至第三，為八成；

translations.literal: again from the second to the third was eight movements;
translations.idiomatic: again from the second to the third was eight movements;

sentences.zh: 若九變者，又從第三至北第一，為九變。

translations.literal: for nine changes, again from the third to the first northern marker made nine changes.
translations.idiomatic: for nine changes, again from the third to the first northern marker completed the nine changes.

sentences.zh: 執麾一人，從協律郎以麾舉偃而節樂。

translations.literal: One banner-pole bearer followed the Pitch-Pipe Master, raising and lowering the banner to mark the music.
translations.idiomatic: One banner-pole bearer followed the Pitch-Pipe Master, raising and lowering the banner to regulate the music.

sentences.zh: 照燭二人，掌執籠燭而節樂。

translations.literal: Two torchbearers were charged with holding caged candles to mark the music.
translations.idiomatic: Two torchbearers held caged candles to regulate when the music began and ended.

sentences.zh: 凡樂作止，皆舉偃其籠燭。

translations.literal: Whenever music began or stopped, they raised or lowered their caged candles.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever music began or stopped, they raised or lowered their caged candles.

sentences.zh: 一人立於堂上門東，視殿內獻官禮節，麾燭以示縣間。

translations.literal: One stood east of the hall gate above, watching the offering-official's ritual inside the hall and waving the candles to signal those between the ensembles.
translations.idiomatic: One stood east of the hall gate above, watching the offering-official's ritual inside and waving the candles to signal those between the ensembles.

sentences.zh: 一人立於堂下縣間，俟三獻入導初獻至位，立於其左。

translations.literal: One stood between the ensembles below the hall, waiting until the three offering-officials entered, then guided the first offering-official to his place and stood at his left.
translations.idiomatic: One stood between the ensembles below, and when the three offering-officials entered, guided the first to his station and stood at his left.

sentences.zh: （初獻行，皆前導，亞、終則否。）〉

translations.literal: (For the first offering-official's procession, all led the way; for the second and final offerings, they did not.)
translations.idiomatic: (They led the way for the first offering-official's procession, but not for the second or final offerings.)

sentences.zh: 凡殿下禮節，則麾其燭以示上下。

translations.literal: For every ritual below the hall, they waved their candles to signal above and below.
translations.idiomatic: For every ritual below the hall, they waved their candles to signal above and below.

sentences.zh: 初獻詣盥洗位，乃偃其燭，止亦如之。

translations.literal: When the first offering-official went to the ablution station, they lowered their candles; stopping the music was done likewise.
translations.idiomatic: When the first offering-official went to the ablution station, they lowered their candles; stopping the music worked the same way.

sentences.zh: 俟初獻動為節，宮縣樂作，詣盥洗位，洗拭瓚訖，樂止。

translations.literal: Waiting for the first offering-official's movement as the signal, the court ensemble began; he went to the ablution station, washed and wiped the libation vessel clean, and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the first offering-official moved, the court ensemble began; he went to the ablution station, washed and wiped the libation vessel, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 詣階，登歌樂作，升自東階，至殿門，樂止，乃立於陛側以俟。

translations.literal: Approaching the steps, ascending-hall music began; he ascended by the eastern steps to the hall gate, the music stopped, and he stood beside the steps to wait.
translations.idiomatic: As he approached the steps, ascending-hall music began; he ascended the eastern steps to the hall gate, the music stopped, and he waited beside the steps.

sentences.zh: 晨稞訖，初獻出殿，登歌樂作，至版位，樂止。

translations.literal: When the morning grain offering was complete, the first offering-official left the hall; ascending-hall music began until he reached the spirit tablet station, then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the morning grain offering was finished, the first offering-official left the hall; ascending-hall music played until he reached the spirit-tablet station, then stopped.

sentences.zh: 司徒迎饌至橫街，轉身北向，宮縣樂作，司徒奉俎至各室遍奠訖，樂止。

translations.literal: The Minister of Education welcomed the offerings to the cross street, turned north, the court ensemble began; he bore the trays to each chamber and presented offerings throughout, then the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Education brought the offerings to the cross street, turned north, and the court ensemble began; he bore the trays to each chamber and presented offerings throughout, then the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 酌獻，初獻詣盥洗位，宮縣樂作，詣爵洗位，洗拭爵訖，樂止。

translations.literal: For libation offerings, the first offering-official went to the ablution station; the court ensemble began; he went to the goblet-washing station, washed and wiped the goblet clean, and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: For the libation offering, the first offering-official went to the ablution station while the court ensemble played; he then went to the goblet-washing station, washed and wiped the goblet, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 出笏，登歌樂作，升自東階，至殿門，樂止。

translations.literal: He withdrew his tablet; ascending-hall music began; he ascended by the eastern steps to the hall gate, and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew his tablet; ascending-hall music began as he ascended the eastern steps to the hall gate, then stopped.

sentences.zh: 初獻至酒尊所，酌訖，宮縣樂作，詣神位前，祭酒訖，拜、興、讀祝，樂止。

translations.literal: The first offering-official reached the wine vessels, poured the libation, the court ensemble began; he went before the spirit seat, completed the libation, bowed, rose, and read the prayer—the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The first offering-official reached the wine vessels and poured; the court ensemble began as he went before the spirit seat, offered the libation, bowed, rose, and read the prayer, then the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 讀訖，樂作，再拜訖，樂止。

translations.literal: When the reading was finished, music began; when the double bow was finished, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the reading was finished, music began; when the double bow was complete, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 次詣每室，作止如初。

translations.literal: Next he went to each chamber; starting and stopping were as before.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to each chamber, with music starting and stopping as before.

sentences.zh: 每室各奏本室樂曲，俱獻畢，還至殿門，登歌樂作，降自東階，至版位，樂止。

translations.literal: Each chamber played its own chamber's melody; when all offerings were complete, he returned to the hall gate; ascending-hall music began; he descended by the eastern steps to the spirit tablet station, and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Each chamber played its own melody; when all offerings were complete, he returned to the hall gate; ascending-hall music played as he descended the eastern steps to the spirit-tablet station, then stopped.

sentences.zh: 文舞退，武舞進，宮縣樂作，舞者立定，樂止。

translations.literal: The civil dance withdrew and the martial dance entered; the court ensemble began; when the dancers stood in place, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The civil dancers withdrew and the martial dancers entered; the court ensemble began, and when the dancers stood in place, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 亞獻行禮，無節步之樂，至酒尊所，酌酒訖，出笏，宮縣樂作，詣神位前，奠獻畢，樂止。

translations.literal: The second offering-official performed the rite without music marking his steps; reaching the wine vessels, he poured the wine, withdrew his tablet, the court ensemble began; he went before the spirit seat and completed the presentation, and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The second offering-official performed the rite without music marking his steps; at the wine vessels he poured, withdrew his tablet, and the court ensemble began as he went before the spirit seat and completed the presentation, then the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 次詣每室，作止如初。

translations.literal: Next he went to each chamber; starting and stopping were as before.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to each chamber, with music starting and stopping as before.

sentences.zh: 俱畢，還至版位，皆無樂。

translations.literal: When all was finished, he returned to the spirit tablet station—all without music.
translations.idiomatic: When all was finished, he returned to the spirit-tablet station without music.

sentences.zh: 終獻樂作，同亞獻，助奠以下升殿，奠馬湩，至神位，蒙古巫祝致詞訖，宮縣樂作，同司徒進饌之曲，禮畢，樂止。

translations.literal: Music for the final offering began, the same as for the second; assistant presenters and those below ascended the hall, presented mare's milk; reaching the spirit seat, the Mongol shaman finished his invocation; the court ensemble began with the same piece as when the Minister of Education brought the offerings; when the rite was complete, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Music for the final offering began, as for the second; assistant presenters ascended the hall and presented mare's milk; at the spirit seat the Mongol shaman finished his invocation; the court ensemble played the same piece as when the Minister of Education brought the offerings, and when the rite was complete, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 出殿，登歌樂作，各復位，樂止。

translations.literal: Leaving the hall, ascending-hall music began; each returned to his place, and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: As they left the hall, ascending-hall music began; each returned to his station, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 太祝徹籩豆，登歌樂作，卒徹，樂止。

translations.literal: The Grand Invoker removed the baskets and stands; ascending-hall music began; when removal was complete, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Invoker removed the baskets and stands while ascending-hall music played; when removal was complete, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 奉禮贊拜，眾官皆再拜訖，送神，宮縣樂作，一成而止。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies prompted the bow; all officials completed their double bows; seeing off the spirits, the court ensemble began and stopped after one movement.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies prompted the bow; all officials bowed twice; as the spirits were sent off, the court ensemble played one movement and stopped.

sentences.zh: 宴樂之器

translations.literal: Banquet Music Instruments
translations.idiomatic: Banquet Music Instruments

sentences.zh: 興隆笙，制以楠木，形如夾屏，上銳而面平，縷金雕鏤枇杷、寶相、孔雀、竹木、雲氣，兩旁側立花板，居背三之一，中為虛櫃，如笙之匏。

translations.literal: The Prosperity sheng was made of nanmu wood, shaped like a folding screen, sharp above and flat-faced, with gold filigree and carving of loquat, treasure-flower, peacock, bamboo, trees, and cloud vapors; flower panels stood on either side, occupying one-third of the back; in the center was a hollow cabinet like the gourd of a sheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Prosperity sheng was made of nanmu wood in the shape of a folding screen, sharp above and flat-faced, with gold filigree and carvings of loquat, treasure-flowers, peacocks, bamboo, trees, and clouds. Flower panels stood on either side, occupying a third of the back; at the center was a hollow cabinet like a sheng's gourd.

sentences.zh: 上豎紫竹管九十，管端實以木蓮苞。

translations.literal: Ninety purple bamboo pipes were set upright upon it, their ends stopped with lotus-wood buds.
translations.idiomatic: Ninety purple bamboo pipes rose from it, their ends stopped with lotus-wood buds.

sentences.zh: 櫃外出小橛十五，上豎小管，管端實以銅杏葉。

translations.literal: Outside the cabinet projected fifteen small pegs, each bearing a small pipe stopped at the end with a copper apricot leaf.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen small pegs projected outside the cabinet, each bearing a small pipe stopped with a copper apricot leaf.

sentences.zh: 下有座，獅象繞之，座上櫃前立花板一，雕鏤如背，板間出二皮風口，用則設朱漆小架於座前，系風囊於風口，囊面如琵琶，朱漆雜花，有柄，一人挼小管，一人鼓風囊，則簧自隨調而鳴。

translations.literal: Below was a stand encircled by lions and elephants; before the cabinet on the stand stood one flower panel, carved like the back; between the panels were two leather wind openings. In use, a small vermilion-lacquered frame was set before the stand, a wind bladder tied to the openings; the bladder's face was like a pipa, vermilion lacquer with mixed flowers, with a handle; one person plucked the small pipes, one person pumped the wind bladder, and the reeds sounded according to the mode.
translations.idiomatic: It stood on a base ringed with lions and elephants; before the cabinet on the base stood a flower panel carved like the back, with two leather wind openings between the panels. In performance a small vermilion-lacquered frame was set before the base and a wind bladder—shaped like a pipa, lacquered vermilion with floral patterns and fitted with a handle—was tied to the openings. One player plucked the small pipes while another pumped the bladder, and the reeds sounded in the chosen mode.

sentences.zh: 中統間，回回國所進。

translations.literal: During the Zhongtong era it was presented by the Muslim countries.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhongtong era it was presented from the Muslim lands.

sentences.zh: 以竹為簧，有聲而無律。

translations.literal: Its reeds were of bamboo; it had sound but no pitch-standard.
translations.idiomatic: Its reeds were bamboo; it produced sound but no fixed pitch.

sentences.zh: 玉宸樂院判官鄭秀乃考音律，分定清濁，增改如今制。

translations.literal: Zheng Xiu, judge of the Jade Hall Music Academy, then examined pitch and mode, distinguished clear and muddy tones, and enlarged and revised it into the present form.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xiu, judge of the Jade Hall Music Academy, then examined pitch and mode, distinguished clear from muddy tones, and revised it into its present form.

sentences.zh: 其在殿上者，盾頭兩旁立刻木孔雀二，飾以真孔雀羽，中設機。

translations.literal: The hall version had two carved wooden peacocks set on either side of the shield-head, adorned with real peacock feathers, with a mechanism between them.
translations.idiomatic: The hall version had two carved wooden peacocks flanking the shield-head, adorned with real peacock feathers, with a mechanism between them.

sentences.zh: 每奏，工三人，一人鼓風囊，一人按律，一人運動其機，則孔雀飛舞應節。

translations.literal: At each performance three workers: one pumped the wind bladder, one held the pitch, one worked the mechanism, and the peacocks danced in time with the beat.
translations.idiomatic: At each performance three players took part: one pumped the wind bladder, one held the pitch, and one worked the mechanism, so that the peacocks danced in time with the music.

sentences.zh: 殿庭笙十，延祐間增制，不用孔雀。

translations.literal: Ten hall-court sheng were added during the Yanyou era, without peacocks.
translations.idiomatic: Ten hall-court sheng were added during the Yanyou era, without the peacock mechanism.

sentences.zh: 琵琶，制以木，曲首，長頸，四軫，頸有品，闊面，四弦，面飾雜花。

translations.literal: The pipa was made of wood, with a curved head, long neck, four pegs, frets on the neck, broad face, four strings, and the face decorated with mixed flowers.
translations.idiomatic: The pipa was of wood, with a curved head, long neck, four pegs, frets on the neck, a broad soundboard, four strings, and a face decorated with floral patterns.

sentences.zh: 箏，如瑟，兩頭微垂，有柱，十三弦。

translations.literal: The zheng was like the se, with both ends slightly drooping, bridges, and thirteen strings.
translations.idiomatic: The zheng resembled the se, with both ends slightly drooping, bridges, and thirteen strings.

sentences.zh: 火不思，制如琵琶，直頸，無品，有小槽，圓腹如半瓶榼，以皮為面，四弦，皮絣同一孤柱。

translations.literal: The huobusi was made like the pipa, with a straight neck, no frets, a small groove, a round belly like half a bottle-flask, a skin face, four strings, and the skin laced to a single bridge.
translations.idiomatic: The huobusi resembled the pipa but had a straight neck without frets, a small groove, a round belly like half a flask, a skin soundboard, four strings, and the skin laced to a single bridge.

sentences.zh: 胡琴，制如火不思，卷頸，龍首，二弦，用弓捩之，弓之弦以馬尾。

translations.literal: The huqin was made like the huobusi, with a curled neck, dragon head, two strings, played with a bow twisted across them; the bow's string was of horsehair.
translations.idiomatic: The huqin resembled the huobusi, with a curled neck and dragon head, two strings played with a bow, and horsehair for the bowstring.

sentences.zh: 方響，制以鐵，十六枚，懸於磬虡，小角槌二。

translations.literal: The fangxiang was made of iron, sixteen pieces, suspended on a chime-stone frame, with two small horn mallets.
translations.idiomatic: The fangxiang was of iron—sixteen pieces suspended on a chime-stone frame, with two small horn mallets.

sentences.zh: 廷中設，下施小交足幾，黃羅銷金衣。

translations.literal: It was set up in the court, with a small crossed-leg stand beneath, and a yellow gauze cover with cut-gold pattern.
translations.idiomatic: It was set up in the court on a small crossed-leg stand, with a yellow gauze cover worked in cut gold.

sentences.zh: 龍笛，制如笛，七孔，橫吹之，管首制龍頭，銜同心結帶。

translations.literal: The dragon flute was made like the di, with seven holes, blown horizontally; the pipe head was fashioned as a dragon head holding a knotted cord of concentric circles.
translations.idiomatic: The dragon flute resembled the di, with seven holes and played horizontally; its head was carved as a dragon holding a knotted cord of concentric circles.

sentences.zh: 頭管，制以竹為管，卷蘆葉為首，竅七。

translations.literal: The touguan was made with a bamboo pipe, a reed-leaf rolled for the head, and seven holes.
translations.idiomatic: The touguan had a bamboo pipe with a rolled reed-leaf head and seven holes.

sentences.zh: 笙，制以匏為底，列管於上，管十三，簧如之。

translations.literal: The sheng was made with a gourd base, pipes arrayed above, thirteen pipes, and reeds to match.
translations.idiomatic: The sheng had a gourd base with pipes arrayed above—thirteen pipes, each with its reed.

sentences.zh: 箜篌，制以木，闊腹，腹下施橫木，而加軫二十四，柱頭及首並加鳳喙。

translations.literal: The konghou was made of wood, with a broad belly; a crossbar was set beneath the belly, and twenty-four pegs were added; the pillar head and top both bore phoenix beaks.
translations.idiomatic: The konghou was of wood with a broad belly; a crossbar beneath the belly bore twenty-four pegs, and both the pillar head and the top were capped with phoenix beaks.

sentences.zh: 雲敖，制以銅，為小鑼十三，同一木架，下有長柄，左手持，而右手以小槌擊之。

translations.literal: The yun'ao was made of copper, thirteen small gongs on one wooden frame, with a long handle below; the left hand held it while the right hand struck with a small mallet.
translations.idiomatic: The yun'ao was of copper—thirteen small gongs on one wooden frame with a long handle below; the player held it in the left hand and struck with a small mallet in the right.

sentences.zh: 簫，制如笛，五孔。

translations.literal: The xiao was made like the di, with five holes.
translations.idiomatic: The xiao resembled the di, with five holes.

sentences.zh: 戲竹，制如籈，長二尺餘，上系流蘇香囊，執而偃之，以止樂。

translations.literal: The xizhu was made like the zhu, more than two feet long, with tassels and a scent pouch tied above; held upraised and then lowered to stop the music.
translations.idiomatic: The xizhu resembled the zhu, more than two feet long, with tassels and a scent pouch tied above; the player raised and lowered it to stop the music.

sentences.zh: 鼓，制以木為匡，冒以革，朱漆雜花，面繪復身龍，長竿二。

translations.literal: The drum was made with a wooden frame, covered with hide, vermilion lacquer with mixed flowers, the face painted with a coiled dragon, and two long poles.
translations.idiomatic: The drum had a wooden frame covered with hide, vermilion lacquer with floral patterns, a face painted with a coiled dragon, and two long poles.

sentences.zh: 廷中設，則有大木架，又有擊撾高座。

translations.literal: When set up in the court, there was a large wooden frame, and also a high seat for striking.
translations.idiomatic: In the court it stood on a large wooden frame, with a high seat for the striker.

sentences.zh: 杖鼓，制以木為匡，細腰，以皮冒之，上施五彩繡帶，右擊以杖，左拍以手。

translations.literal: The zhanggu was made with a wooden frame, a narrow waist, covered with hide, with five-colored embroidered bands above; struck with a stick in the right hand and clapped with the left.
translations.idiomatic: The zhanggu had a wooden frame and narrow waist, was covered with hide, and bore five-colored embroidered bands; the player struck it with a stick in the right hand and clapped with the left.

sentences.zh: 劄鼓，制如杖鼓而小，左持而右擊之。

translations.literal: The zhagu was made like the zhanggu but smaller, held in the left hand and struck with the right.
translations.idiomatic: The zhagu resembled the zhanggu but smaller, held in the left hand and struck with the right.

sentences.zh: 和鼓，制如大鼓而小，左持而右擊之。

translations.literal: The hegu was made like the large drum but smaller, held in the left hand and struck with the right.
translations.idiomatic: The hegu resembled the large drum but smaller, held in the left hand and struck with the right.

sentences.zh: 闉，制如箏而七弦，有柱，用竹軋之。

translations.literal: The yin was made like the zheng but with seven strings, with bridges, played by plucking with bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: The yin resembled the zheng but had seven strings and bridges, and was played by plucking with bamboo.

sentences.zh: 羌笛，制如笛而長，三孔。

translations.literal: The Qiang flute was made like the di but longer, with three holes.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang flute resembled the di but was longer, with three holes.

sentences.zh: 拍板，制以木為板，以繩聯之。

translations.literal: The paiban was made of wooden boards joined by cord.
translations.idiomatic: The paiban consisted of wooden boards joined by cord.

sentences.zh: 水盞，制以銅，凡十有二，擊以鐵箸。

translations.literal: The shuizhan was made of copper, twelve in all, struck with iron chopsticks.
translations.idiomatic: The shuizhan was of copper—twelve in all—struck with iron chopsticks.

sentences.zh: 樂音王隊：

translations.literal: The Music-King Formation:
translations.idiomatic: The Music-King Formation:

sentences.zh: （元旦用之。）〉

translations.literal: (Used at New Year's Day.)
translations.idiomatic: (Used on New Year's Day.)

sentences.zh: 引隊大樂禮官二員，冠展角襆頭，紫袍，塗金帶，執笏。

translations.literal: Leading the formation: two ritual officers of Great Music, wearing extended-corner futou, purple robes, gilt belts, and holding tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Leading the formation were two ritual officers of Great Music in extended-corner futou, purple robes, gilt belts, and tablets.

sentences.zh: 次執戲竹二人，同前服。

translations.literal: Next, two xizhu bearers, in the same dress as above.
translations.idiomatic: Next came two xizhu bearers in the same dress.

sentences.zh: 次樂工八人，冠花襆頭。

translations.literal: Next, eight musicians, wearing floral futou,
translations.idiomatic: Next came eight musicians in floral futou,

sentences.zh: 紫窄衫，銅束帶。

translations.literal: purple narrow jackets, and copper belts.
translations.idiomatic: purple narrow jackets, and copper belts.

sentences.zh: 龍笛三，杖鼓三，金鞚小鼓一，板一，奏《萬年歡》之曲。

translations.literal: three dragon flutes, three zhanggu, one small golden-bridle drum, and one paiban, playing the melody 《Ten Thousand Years of Joy》.
translations.idiomatic: with three dragon flutes, three zhanggu, one small golden-bridle drum, and one paiban, playing 《Ten Thousand Years of Joy》.

sentences.zh: 從東階升，至御前，以次而西，折繞而南，北向立。

translations.literal: They ascended by the eastern steps to before the throne, then in order westward, turned and wound southward, and stood facing north.
translations.idiomatic: They ascended the eastern steps to the throne, moved west in order, turned south, and stood facing north.

sentences.zh: （後隊進，皆仿此。）〉

translations.literal: (Later formations entered, all following this pattern.)
translations.idiomatic: (Later formations entered following this same pattern.)

sentences.zh: 次二隊，婦女十人，冠展角襆頭，紫袍，隨樂聲進至御前，分左右相向立。

translations.literal: Next, the second formation: ten women, wearing extended-corner futou and purple robes, advanced with the music to before the throne and stood facing one another to left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Next came a formation of ten women in extended-corner futou and purple robes, who advanced with the music to the throne and stood facing one another to left and right.

sentences.zh: 次婦女一人，冠唐帽，黃袍，進北向立定，樂止，念致語畢，樂作，奏《長春柳》之曲。

translations.literal: Next, one woman, wearing a Tang cap and yellow robe, advanced, stood facing north, the music stopped, she finished the congratulatory address, music began, and they played 《Long Spring Willow》.
translations.idiomatic: Next one woman in a Tang cap and yellow robe advanced, stood facing north, finished the congratulatory address as the music stopped, then the music resumed with 《Long Spring Willow》.

sentences.zh: 次三隊，男子三人，戴紅發青面具，雜彩衣，次一人，冠唐帽，綠襕袍，角帶，舞蹈而進，立於前隊之右。

translations.literal: Next, the third formation: three men wearing red-haired green masks and mixed-color dress; next one man in a Tang cap, green round-collared robe, and horn belt, dancing forward to stand at the right of the preceding formation.
translations.idiomatic: Next came three men in red-haired green masks and motley dress, followed by one man in a Tang cap, green round-collared robe, and horn belt, who danced forward to stand at the right of the preceding formation.

sentences.zh: 次四隊，男子一人，戴孔雀明王像面具，披金甲，執叉，從者二人，戴毗沙神像面具，紅袍，執斧。

translations.literal: Next, the fourth formation: one man wearing a Peacock Bright-King mask, clad in golden armor and holding a fork; two attendants wearing Vaisravana masks, red robes, holding axes.
translations.idiomatic: Next came one man wearing a Peacock Bright-King mask, clad in golden armor and holding a fork, with two attendants in Vaisravana masks, red robes, and axes.

sentences.zh: 次五隊，男子五人，冠五梁冠，戴龍王面具，繡氅，執圭，與前隊同進，北向立。

translations.literal: Next, the fifth formation: five men wearing five-ridge caps, Dragon-King masks, embroidered mantles, holding scepters; they advanced with the preceding formation and stood facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Next came five men in five-ridge caps and Dragon-King masks, embroidered mantles, and scepters, who advanced with the preceding formation and stood facing north.

sentences.zh: 次六隊，男子五人，為飛天夜叉之像，舞蹈以進。

translations.literal: Next, the sixth formation: five men as images of flying apsaras and yakshas, dancing forward.
translations.idiomatic: Next came five men costumed as flying apsaras and yakshas, dancing forward.

sentences.zh: 次七隊，樂工八人，冠霸王冠，青面具，錦繡衣，龍笛三，觱栗三，杖鼓二，與前大樂合奏《吉利牙》之曲。

translations.literal: Next, the seventh formation: eight musicians wearing Overlord caps, green masks, and brocade dress; three dragon flutes, three suona, two zhanggu; together with the preceding Great Music they played 《Jiliya》.
translations.idiomatic: Next came eight musicians in Overlord caps, green masks, and brocade dress, with three dragon flutes, three suona, and two zhanggu, joining the preceding Great Music in 《Jiliya》.

sentences.zh: 次八隊，婦女二十人，冠廣翠冠，銷金綠衣，執牡丹花，舞唱前曲，與樂聲相和，進至御前，北向，列為九重，重四人，曲終，再起，與後隊相和。

translations.literal: Next, the eighth formation: twenty women wearing broad emerald crowns, cut-gold green robes, holding peonies, dancing and singing the preceding melody in harmony with the music; advancing to before the throne, facing north, arrayed in nine ranks of four each; when the piece ended they rose again in harmony with the following formation.
translations.idiomatic: Next came twenty women in broad emerald crowns and cut-gold green robes, holding peonies and dancing and singing in time with the music. They advanced to the throne, faced north in nine ranks of four, and when the piece ended rose again in harmony with the following formation.

sentences.zh: 次九隊，婦女二十人，冠金梳翠花鈿，繡衣，執花鞚稍子鼓，舞唱前曲，與前隊相和。

translations.literal: Next, the ninth formation: twenty women wearing gold-comb and emerald-flower hairpins, embroidered robes, holding floral-bridle shao drums, dancing and singing the preceding melody in harmony with the preceding formation.
translations.idiomatic: Next came twenty women with gold-comb and emerald-flower hairpins, embroidered robes, and floral-bridle shao drums, dancing and singing in harmony with the preceding formation.

sentences.zh: 次十隊，婦女八人，花髻，服銷金桃紅衣，搖日月金鞚稍子鼓，舞唱同前。

translations.literal: Next, the tenth formation: eight women with floral topknots, cut-gold peach-pink robes, shaking sun-and-moon golden-bridle shao drums, dancing and singing as before.
translations.idiomatic: Next came eight women with floral topknots, cut-gold peach-pink robes, and sun-and-moon golden-bridle shao drums, dancing and singing as before.

sentences.zh: 次男子五人，作五方菩薩梵像，搖日月鼓。

translations.literal: Next, five men as images of the Five-Direction Bodhisattvas in Sanskrit style, shaking sun-and-moon drums.
translations.idiomatic: Next came five men costumed as the Five-Direction Bodhisattvas in Sanskrit style, shaking sun-and-moon drums.

sentences.zh: 次一人，作樂音王菩薩梵像，執花鞚稍子鼓，齊聲舞前曲一闋，樂止。

translations.literal: Next, one man as the Music-King Bodhisattva in Sanskrit style, holding a floral-bridle shao drum; all together danced and sang one stanza of the preceding melody, then the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Next came one man as the Music-King Bodhisattva in Sanskrit style, holding a floral-bridle shao drum; all together danced and sang one stanza of the preceding melody, then the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 次婦女三人，歌《新水令》、《沽美酒》、《太平令》之曲終，念口號畢，舞唱相和，以次而出。

translations.literal: Next, three women sang through 《New Water Tune》, 《Buying Fine Wine》, and 《Peace Command》; when the slogans were finished they danced and sang in harmony and withdrew in order.
translations.idiomatic: Finally three women sang through 《New Water Tune》, 《Buying Fine Wine》, and 《Peace Command》; when the slogans were finished they danced and sang together and withdrew in order.

sentences.zh: 壽星隊：

translations.literal: The Longevity Star Formation:
translations.idiomatic: The Longevity Star Formation:

sentences.zh: （天壽節用之。）〉

translations.literal: (Used at the Heavenly Longevity Festival.)
translations.idiomatic: (Used at the Heavenly Longevity Festival.)

sentences.zh: 引隊禮官樂工大樂冠服，並同樂音王隊。

translations.literal: The leading formation's ritual officers, musicians, and Great Music caps and dress were all the same as the Music-King Formation.
translations.idiomatic: The leading ritual officers, musicians, and Great Music dress matched the Music-King Formation.

sentences.zh: 次二隊，婦女十人，冠唐巾，服銷金紫衣，銅束帶。

translations.literal: Next, the second formation: ten women wearing Tang caps, cut-gold purple robes, and copper belts.
translations.idiomatic: Next came ten women in Tang caps, cut-gold purple robes, and copper belts.

sentences.zh: 次婦女一人，冠平天冠，服繡鶴氅，方心曲領，執圭，以次進至御前，立定，樂止，念致語畢，樂作，奏《長春柳》之曲。

translations.literal: Next, one woman wearing a Level-Heaven crown, embroidered crane mantle, square-heart curved collar, holding a scepter; advancing in order to before the throne, standing in place, music stopped, congratulatory address finished, music began, playing 《Long Spring Willow》.
translations.idiomatic: Next one woman in a Level-Heaven crown, embroidered crane mantle, square-heart curved collar, and scepter advanced to the throne, finished the congratulatory address as the music stopped, then the music resumed with 《Long Spring Willow》.

sentences.zh: 次三隊，男子三人，冠服舞蹈，並同樂音王隊。

translations.literal: Next, the third formation: three men; caps, dress, and dance all as in the Music-King Formation.
translations.idiomatic: Next came three men whose caps, dress, and dance matched the Music-King Formation.

sentences.zh: 次四隊，男子一人，冠金漆弁冠，服緋袍，塗金帶，執笏；

translations.literal: Next, the fourth formation: one man wearing a gold-lacquered bian cap, scarlet robe, gilt belt, holding a tablet;
translations.idiomatic: Next came one man in a gold-lacquered bian cap, scarlet robe, gilt belt, and tablet;

sentences.zh: 從者二人，錦帽，繡衣，執金字福祿牌。

translations.literal: two attendants in brocade caps and embroidered robes, holding gold-letter Fortune-and-Emolument plaques.
translations.idiomatic: with two attendants in brocade caps and embroidered robes bearing gold-letter Fortune-and-Emolument plaques.

sentences.zh: 次五隊，男子一人，冠卷雲冠，青面具，綠袍，塗金帶，分執梅、竹、松、椿、石，同前隊而進，北向立。

translations.literal: Next, the fifth formation: one man wearing a curling-cloud crown, green mask, green robe, gilt belt, holding plum, bamboo, pine, paulownia, and stone in turn; advancing with the preceding formation and standing facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Next came one man in a curling-cloud crown, green mask, green robe, and gilt belt, holding plum, bamboo, pine, paulownia, and stone in turn; he advanced with the preceding formation and stood facing north.

sentences.zh: 次六隊，男子五人，為烏鴉之像，作飛舞之態，進立於前隊之左，樂止。

translations.literal: Next, the sixth formation: five men as crow images in flying dance, advancing to stand at the left of the preceding formation; the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Next came five men costumed as crows in flying dance, advancing to stand at the left of the preceding formation, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 次七隊，樂工十有二人，冠雲頭冠，銷金緋袍，白裙，龍笛三，觱栗三，劄鼓三，和鼓一，板一，與前大樂合奏《山荊子》帶《妖神急》之曲。

translations.literal: Next, the seventh formation: twelve musicians wearing cloud-head crowns, cut-gold scarlet robes, white skirts; three dragon flutes, three suona, three zhagu, one hegu, one paiban; together with the preceding Great Music they played 《Mountain Thorn》 with 《Demon Spirit Urgent》.
translations.idiomatic: Next came twelve musicians in cloud-head crowns, cut-gold scarlet robes, and white skirts, with three dragon flutes, three suona, three zhagu, one hegu, and one paiban, joining the preceding Great Music in 《Mountain Thorn》 with 《Demon Spirit Urgent》.

sentences.zh: 次八隊，婦女二十人，冠鳳翹冠，翠花鈿，服寬袖衣，加雲肩、霞綬、玉佩，各執寶蓋，舞唱前曲。

translations.literal: Next, the eighth formation: twenty women wearing phoenix-crest crowns, emerald-flower hairpins, wide-sleeved robes with cloud collars, mist sashes, and jade pendants, each holding a treasure canopy, dancing and singing the preceding melody.
translations.idiomatic: Next came twenty women in phoenix-crest crowns, emerald-flower hairpins, wide-sleeved robes with cloud collars, mist sashes, and jade pendants, each holding a treasure canopy and dancing and singing the preceding melody.

sentences.zh: 次九隊，婦女三十人，冠玉女冠，翠花鈿，服黃銷金寬袖衣，加雲肩、霞綬、玉佩，各執棕毛日月扇，舞唱前曲，與前隊相和。

translations.literal: Next, the ninth formation: thirty women wearing Jade-Maiden crowns, emerald-flower hairpins, yellow cut-gold wide-sleeved robes with cloud collars, mist sashes, and jade pendants, each holding palm-fiber sun-and-moon fans, dancing and singing the preceding melody in harmony with the preceding formation.
translations.idiomatic: Next came thirty women in Jade-Maiden crowns, emerald-flower hairpins, yellow cut-gold wide-sleeved robes with cloud collars, mist sashes, and jade pendants, each with a palm-fiber sun-and-moon fan, dancing and singing in harmony with the preceding formation.

sentences.zh: 次十隊，婦女八人，服雜彩衣，被槲葉、魚鼓、簡子。

translations.literal: Next, the tenth formation: eight women in mixed-color robes, wearing oak leaves, fish drums, and clappers.
translations.idiomatic: Next came eight women in motley robes, wearing oak leaves and carrying fish drums and clappers.

sentences.zh: 次男子八人，冠束發冠，金掩心甲，銷金緋袍，執戟。

translations.literal: Next, eight men wearing bound-hair crowns, gold heart-guarding armor, cut-gold scarlet robes, holding halberds.
translations.idiomatic: Next came eight men in bound-hair crowns, gold heart-guarding armor, cut-gold scarlet robes, and halberds.

sentences.zh: 次為龜鶴之像各一。

translations.literal: Next, one image each of tortoise and crane.
translations.idiomatic: Next came one tortoise figure and one crane figure.

sentences.zh: 次男子五人，冠黑紗帽，服繡鶴氅，朱履，策龍頭濆杖，齊舞唱前曲一闋，樂止。

translations.literal: Next, five men wearing black gauze caps, embroidered crane mantles, red shoes, dragon-head spray staves; all together danced and sang one stanza of the preceding melody, and the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Next came five men in black gauze caps, embroidered crane mantles, red shoes, and dragon-head spray staves, who danced and sang one stanza of the preceding melody together, then the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 次婦女三人，歌《新水令》、《沽美酒》、《太平令》之曲終，念口號畢，舞唱相和，以次而出。

translations.literal: Next, three women sang through 《New Water Tune》, 《Buying Fine Wine》, and 《Peace Command》; when the slogans were finished they danced and sang in harmony and withdrew in order.
translations.idiomatic: Finally three women sang through 《New Water Tune》, 《Buying Fine Wine》, and 《Peace Command》; when the slogans were finished they danced and sang together and withdrew in order.

sentences.zh: 禮樂隊：

translations.literal: The Rites-and-Music Formation:
translations.idiomatic: The Rites-and-Music Formation:

sentences.zh: （朝會用之。）〉

translations.literal: (Used at court assemblies.)
translations.idiomatic: (Used at court assemblies.)

sentences.zh: 引隊禮官樂工大樂冠服，並同樂音王隊。

translations.literal: The leading formation's ritual officers, musicians, and Great Music caps and dress were all the same as the Music-King Formation.
translations.idiomatic: The leading ritual officers, musicians, and Great Music dress matched the Music-King Formation.

sentences.zh: 次二隊，婦女十人，冠黑漆弁冠，服青素袍，方心曲領，白裙，束帶，執圭；

translations.literal: Next, the second formation: ten women wearing black-lacquered bian caps, blue plain robes, square-heart curved collars, white skirts, belts, holding scepters;
translations.idiomatic: Next came ten women in black-lacquered bian caps, blue plain robes, square-heart curved collars, white skirts, belts, and scepters;

sentences.zh: 次婦女一人，冠九龍冠，服繡紅袍，玉束帶，進至御前，立定，樂止，念致語畢，樂作，奏《長春柳》之曲。

translations.literal: next one woman wearing a Nine-Dragon crown, embroidered red robe, jade belt; advancing to before the throne, standing in place, music stopped, congratulatory address finished, music began, playing 《Long Spring Willow》.
translations.idiomatic: then one woman in a Nine-Dragon crown, embroidered red robe, and jade belt advanced to the throne, finished the congratulatory address as the music stopped, then the music resumed with 《Long Spring Willow》.

sentences.zh: 次三隊，男子三人，冠服舞蹈同樂音王隊。

translations.literal: Next, the third formation: three men; caps, dress, and dance as in the Music-King Formation.
translations.idiomatic: Next came three men whose caps, dress, and dance matched the Music-King Formation.

sentences.zh: 次四隊，男子三人，皆冠卷雲冠，服黃袍，塗金帶，執圭。

translations.literal: Next, the fourth formation: three men, all wearing curling-cloud crowns, yellow robes, gilt belts, holding scepters.
translations.idiomatic: Next came three men, all in curling-cloud crowns, yellow robes, gilt belts, and scepters.

sentences.zh: 次五隊，男子五人，皆冠三龍冠，服紅袍，各執劈正金斧，同前隊而進，北向立。

translations.literal: Next, the fifth formation: five men, all wearing Three-Dragon crowns, red robes, each holding a rectifying golden axe; advancing with the preceding formation and standing facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Next came five men in Three-Dragon crowns and red robes, each with a rectifying golden axe, who advanced with the preceding formation and stood facing north.

sentences.zh: 次六隊，童子五人，三髻，素衣，各執香花，舞蹈而進，樂止。

translations.literal: Next, the sixth formation: five boys with triple topknots, plain dress, each holding fragrant flowers, dancing forward; the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Next came five boys with triple topknots and plain dress, each holding fragrant flowers, who danced forward, and the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 次七隊，樂工八人，皆冠束發冠，服錦衣白袍，龍笛三，觱栗三，杖鼓二，與前大樂合奏《新水令》、《水仙子》之曲。

translations.literal: Next, the seventh formation: eight musicians, all wearing bound-hair crowns, brocade jackets and white robes; three dragon flutes, three suona, two zhanggu; together with the preceding Great Music they played 《New Water Tune》 and 《Water Immortal》.
translations.idiomatic: Next came eight musicians in bound-hair crowns, brocade jackets and white robes, with three dragon flutes, three suona, and two zhanggu, joining the preceding Great Music in 《New Water Tune》 and 《Water Immortal》.

sentences.zh: 次八隊，婦女二十人，冠籠巾，服紫袍，金帶，執笏，歌《新水令》之曲，與樂聲相和，進至御前，分為四行，北向立，鞠躬拜，興，舞蹈，叩頭，山呼，就拜，再拜，畢，復趁聲歌《水仙子》之曲一闋，再歌《青山口》之曲，與後隊相和。

translations.literal: Next, the eighth formation: twenty women wearing cage caps, purple robes, gold belts, holding tablets, singing 《New Water Tune》 in harmony with the music; advancing to before the throne, divided into four rows, standing facing north, bowing with bent bodies, rising, dancing, kowtowing, shouting the mountain call, completing the bow, bowing again; when finished, again following the sound they sang one stanza of 《Water Immortal》, then sang 《Green Mountain Pass》, in harmony with the following formation.
translations.idiomatic: Next came twenty women in cage caps, purple robes, gold belts, and tablets, singing 《New Water Tune》 in time with the music. They advanced to the throne in four rows facing north, bowed, rose, danced, kowtowed, shouted the mountain call, completed their bows, and bowed again. Then they sang one stanza of 《Water Immortal》, followed by 《Green Mountain Pass》, in harmony with the following formation.
